rows.note: This is the all-purpose choice for a person who behaves unusually or strangely.

example.english: That person is eccentric and always goes out at three in the morning.
example.traditional: 佢個人好古怪，成日凌晨三點先出街。
example.jyutping: keoi5 go3 jan4 hou3 gu2 gwaai3 seng4 jat6 ling4 san4 saam1 dim2 sin1 ceot1 gaai1

rows.note: This is the all-purpose choice for an eccentric or unusual person, without necessarily being strongly insulting.

example.english: They often go to the beach alone to paint, and everyone calls them an eccentric.
example.traditional: 佢成日一個人去海邊畫畫，大家都話佢係個怪人。
example.jyutping: keoi5 seng4 jat6 jat1 go3 jan4 heoi3 hoi2 bin1 waak6 waa2 daai6 gaa1 dou1 waa6 keoi5 hai6 go3 gwaai3 jan4

rows.note: Use this for a conspicuously bizarre person or kook, with a more insulting tone than 怪人.

example.english: That guy does not eat breakfast until three in the morning; he is a real eccentric.
example.traditional: 嗰條友半夜三點先食早餐，真係個怪胎。
example.jyutping: go2 tiu4 jau5 bun3 je6 saam1 dim2 sin1 sik6 zou2 caan1 zan1 hai6 go3 gwaai3 toi1

rows.note: Use this in geometry or engineering when an object or centre is offset rather than aligned.

example.english: This shaft is slightly eccentric, so it vibrates when it turns.
example.traditional: 呢條軸心有啲偏心，轉起上嚟會震。
example.jyutping: ne1 tiu4 zuk6 sam1 jau5 di1 pin1 sam1 zyun2 hei2 soeng5 lai4 wui5 zan3

rows.note: Use this for a shape that is elliptical rather than a perfect circle.

example.english: This table is eccentric in shape rather than perfectly round.
example.traditional: 呢張枱係橢圓形，唔係正圓形。
example.jyutping: ne1 zoeng1 ci4 hai6 to5 jyun4 jing4 m4 hai6 zing3 jyun4 jing4
